implementation.problem: Kernel MMIO windows reject every overlapping live physical range. Retained boot/VGA windows formerly prevented the full-BAR0 native port, repeated preflight pages and later Booter fuse pages from coexisting.
implementation.mapping: One full measured GA106 BAR0 UC mapping under the common boot-display hold. Eight bounded borrower slots bind API identity, PCI identity, exact BAR resource, chip/revision, stable addresses, monotonic serial and complete returned window stamp. Bounds-checked views carry no unmap handle. Borrowing does not grant register policy, DMA submission or recovery.
implementation.boot_capture: Capture keeps its own lease through PRAMIN snapshot and restoration. All preflight pages, including repeated observation, use the same mapping. A live external borrower prevents reobservation and close before any display/pixel/VRAM resource is released. The narrow PRAMIN write allowlist and aperture-only recovery remain unchanged.
implementation.fuses: Booter security fuse reads borrow the captured BAR0 rather than creating two overlapping windows. Init/shutdown release any retained fuse borrow before closing the capture. Standalone passive probes retain their previous small-window path.
implementation.native_port: openShared uses the exact leased window and validates it during generation/access checks. A possible posted write retains the port lease until its existing native owner establishes quiescence; closing the port never unmaps the parent. Full native execution remains unlinked from main.
implementation.cleanup: Only the mapper unmaps, after the last borrower. Partial/invalid map descriptors are retained; failed unmap and collect are retryable. Moved/stale leases cannot release another owner. Serial survives close/reopen and refuses exhaustion rather than recycling.

validation.coverage: Actual SDK capture + native read-only port + Booter fuse probe share one full mapping. The host map rejects all overlapping ranges like the Kernel. implementation.mapping: Translate a requested CPU physical BAR1 span into one contiguous local VRAM part. Physical mode uses the BAR offset after target/bind/span admission. implementation.admission: Require measured prefetchable BAR span, supported chip, idle BAR1 bind, matching BOOT0/BOOT1, local VRAM instance/tables and the pinned GA106 v2 format. Refuse old format, sparse/unmapped or conflicting leaves, foreign apertures, encryption, privilege/read-only, peer/compression/kind/reserved bits, misalignment and out-of-range descriptors.
implementation.stability: At most7 exact8/16-byte metadata records per translation, reread once in full dependency order. Both control observations must agree. Same live epoch and absolute monotonic deadline checked around each callback; delayed or failed reads cannot publish a result.
implementation.output: Return the translated contiguous part, leaf size, instance span and exact raw dependency path. This is an observation, not a full table backup, retained reservation, recovery token or evidence of GPU quiescence.
implementation.remaining_binding: The real reader must borrow the shared BAR0 owner, serialize/restore PRAMIN access under the held boot display, traverse the whole boot span, retain its table pages and exclude the resolved console/dependencies from firmware allocations. None of these hardware reader or full recovery claims is inferred from host models.

implementation.owner: Drivers/NVIDIA: bar1_reader and boot_mapping linked into explicit boot-check before firmware staging and VRAM reservation. Kernel, SDK and Contract unchanged.
implementation.pf_controls: Verified original physical-function VREG offset 0xb80000, giving BAR1 BLOCK 0xb80f40 and BIND_STATUS 0xb80f50. The old dev_bus alias and unshifted VF offsets are not used for the admitted GA106 function 0.
implementation.reader: Borrow the single retained full BAR0 mapping after a fresh boot/VGA preflight. Exact aligned local-VRAM reads of at most 4 KB within one 1-MB aperture; preserve high window bits, drain writes through the same GPU, and compare exact restoration, identity, epoch and deadline before publishing output. Failure retains the child lease and exact partial window until bounded cleanup succeeds; the parent cannot release meanwhile.
implementation.mapping: Resolve the entire held CPU boot span using the physical/v2 BAR1 walker. Merge consecutive VRAM ranges; preserve every complete 4-KB dependency page, check its observed entries, then reread all full pages and controls. Seal the private backup with a read-only CPU lease and keep it tied to the boot hold.
implementation.reservation: The prepared GSP VRAM lease requires this retained mapping and rejects overlaps between any surface/dependency page and all planned reserved GSP destinations. Its lifetime also blocks mapping/display release while FRTS/run resources remain borrowed. General VRAM allocation remains unavailable.
implementation.boundary: Only the CPU PRAMIN window may change. No BAR1 binding, GPU page-table write, TLB invalidation, VGA relocation, GSP submission or scanout programming. The pre-existing aperture-only recovery is still not full GPU/firmware recovery.

references.pf_registers: TU102 dev_vm.h gives BLOCK 0xf40 and BIND_STATUS 0xf50 relative to VREG. gpuGetVirtRegPhysOffset_TU102 returns DRF_BASE(FULL_PHYS_OFFSET)=0xb80000 for a physical function; only SR-IOV VFs use zero. references.window: Existing pinned GM107 PRAMIN semantics: 0x1700 selects a 1-MB window at BAR0 0x700000, video target 0 and base in 64-KB units. Reader aligns each selected base to 1 MB, preserves high non-window bits, limits copies to 4 KB, and restores the exact previous word before publishing.
